problem: Research and analyze the latest advancements and cutting-edge theories within the field of game design. Specifically include recent developments, research, and practical design applications related to established frameworks like MDA (Mechanics-Dynamics-Aesthetics).
final_response:
<think>...
I will synthesize a structured, data-driven report on recent advancements and cutting-edge theories related to MDA and related frameworks. I will focus on: (1) MDA’s evolving interpretations and extensions (2021), (2) ontology and design methodology perspectives, (3) practical applications in serious games and gamification, and (4) broader design frameworks that integrate player experience. I will avoid unsupported claims and only cite the sources I already have.
</think>

<answer>Introduction and scope
The MDA framework—mechanics, dynamics, aesthetics—remains a foundational lens for analyzing and designing games, with ongoing scholarly work aimed at clarifying its concepts and usability. Recent analyses emphasize that games are artifacts defined by their behavior rather than media, supporting design-centric thinking and clearer analysis in development contexts<cite id="20">MDA defines mechanics as rules and actions, dynamics as run-time behavior, and aesthetics as emotional responses; games are artifacts whose content is behavior</cite>. At the same time, researchers have proposed refinements to make MDA more accessible and useful for designers, framing these efforts within broader ontological goals for game design<cite id="30">The paper positions MDA as the closest approach to a unified ontology and proposes Redefining the MDA (RMDA) to better serve designers</cite>.

Recent refinements and extensions of MDA
A 2021 study redefines MDA’s taxonomy (RMDA) to make the framework more understandable and actionable for designers. The authors argue that an ontology for game design can enhance both understanding and structured methodology, and they clarify MDA’s components with the intent of improving how mechanics, dynamics, and aesthetics are defined and applied in practice<cite id="30">RMDA clarifies MDA’s main components and provides examples to make the tool more usable for designers</cite>. This aligns with earlier descriptions of MDA that stress aligning mechanics and dynamics to evoke desired aesthetics, underscoring the framework’s continued relevance in design thinking<cite id="20">MDA emphasizes designing mechanics and dynamics to invoke the intended aesthetics</cite>.

MDA in practice: serious games and gamification
Beyond theoretical refinements, MDA has been applied in evaluation and design for serious contexts. A dissertation on evaluating serious games proposes a new perspective that complements traditional analysis methods, reflecting the need for frameworks that capture both behavior and experiential outcomes in educational and training settings<cite id="21">The work outlines groundwork for a new evaluation perspective for serious games</cite>. In organizational contexts, the Game-based System Design Framework (GSDF) explicitly uses MDA-inspired elements—mechanics, dynamics, and aesthetics—to design game-based information systems that align with organizational goals and user motivations<cite id="31">GSDF selects game elements to support aesthetics, dynamics, and mechanics to encourage intrinsic or extrinsic motivation</cite>. These applications demonstrate how MDA’s structure can be adapted to non-entertainment domains while maintaining its core analytical utility<cite id="20">MDA supports clearer design choices and analysis at all development levels</cite>.

Broader design frameworks and player experience
While MDA focuses on behavior and emotional responses, complementary frameworks emphasize player experience and motivation. The GSDF explicitly ties mechanics and dynamics to intrinsic and extrinsic motivation, illustrating how design frameworks integrate experiential goals beyond Hunicke’s PEG in practical system design<cite id="31">Designers encourage intrinsic or extrinsic motivation by aligning game-based elements to aesthetics, dynamics, and mechanics</cite>. In entertainment design, recent theses highlight player experience as a central concern and show how best practices in player experience can be derived from design typologies and engagement considerations, reinforcing the importance of aligning mechanics to desired experiential outcomes<cite id="2">A literature review and text mining analysis confirm multiple player types and the role of engagement and challenge in player experience</cite>.

Implications and future directions
The evolving interpretations of MDA suggest a trajectory toward more designer-centric ontologies that clarify how mechanics produce dynamics that invoke aesthetics, while extending the framework’s reach into serious games and gamification<cite id="30">RMDA aims to make MDA more understandable and useful for designers</cite><cite id="21">Evaluation approaches for serious games indicate a need for behavior-and-experience-aligned methods</cite><cite id="31">GSDF adapts MDA elements to organizational contexts</cite>. At the same time, integrating player experience and motivational goals into design processes strengthens the link between mechanics and player outcomes, supporting both entertainment and applied domains<cite id="20">MDA links mechanics/dynamics to aesthetics (emotional responses)</cite><cite id="31">Mechanics/dynamics/aesthetics are used to motivate players in game-based systems</cite>.

Conclusion
MDA remains a robust foundation for game design, with recent work refining its taxonomy and expanding its applicability to serious games and gamification. raw_output.raw_text: <search query="MDA framework game design limitations extensions 2020 2021 2022 2023 2024" search_time="2026年5月21日12时27分星期四"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:9"><title>Redefining the MDA Framework—The Pursuit of a Game Design Ontology</title><summary>In computer science, an ontology is a way of showing the properties of a subject area and how they are related by defining a set of concepts and categories that represent the subject. There have been many attempts to create a widely accepted ontology for the universe of games. Most of these attempts are defined based on an analytical perspective: few have found frequent use outside universities, as they are not easily translated to the development of games, which is a design perspective. There are some core aspects of the domain that turn this task into a difficult goal to achieve. In addition, game designers tend to refuse a methodology or a structured way of developing a game; the main concern is that it can impair creativity in a field that could not survive without it. A defined ontology would improve and mature the growing industry of digital games, both by enhancing the understanding of the domain and by supporting a structured methodology for designing games. This paper describes the properties of digital games and shows how they make it difficult to create an ontology for that field of study, especially when it comes to a design perspective. It clarifies the closest approach to a unified ontology that there is for the game domain: the mechanics, dynamics and aesthetics framework (MDA). We propose the redefinition of MDA’s taxonomy, calling it Redefining the MDA (RMDA), providing better use for the approach from a designer’s perspective, embracing the design properties of the domain, and overcoming issues found in the literature of the game domain. The main purpose of this paper is to clarify the MDA framework by redefining its main components, mechanics, dynamics and aesthetics, as a way to make the tool more understandable and useful for game designers. Understanding aesthetics and how developers can invoke them by correctly defining mechanics and creating dynamics is the main focus of the paper. Thus, some examples are provided in order to explain the applicability of the RMDA as a methodology to produce games.</summary><hostname>MDPI</hostname><publisher>Information</publisher><author_list><author name="Rogrio Junior" affiliation="Department of Arts, University of Beira Interior, Rua Marquês d’Ávila e Bolama, 6201-001 Covilhã, Portugal" /><author name="Frutuoso Silva" affiliation="Department of Computer Science, University of Beira Interior, Rua Marquês d’Ávila e Bolama, 6201-001 Covilhã, Portugal; Instituto de Telecomunicações, University of Beira Interior, Calçada Fonte do Lameiro, 6201-001 Covilhã, Portugal" /></author_list><url>https://www.mdpi.com/2078-2489/12/10/395/pdf?version=1634724367</url><publish_time>2021年9月26日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:10"><title>Intentional Technology For Teaching Practice</title><hostname>AFIT Scholar</hostname><publisher>AFIT Scholar</publisher><author_list><author name="Mike Frick" affiliation="School of Systems & Logistics, Air Force Institute of Technology" /><author name="Aaron V Glassburner" affiliation="Air Force Institute of Technology" /><author name="Jose Gutierrez Del Arroyo" affiliation="Air Force Institute of Technology" /><author name="Rick Kappel" affiliation="Civil Engineering School, Air Force Institute of Technology" /></author_list><url>https://scholar.afit.edu/context/docs/article/1103/viewcontent/AFIT_FLC_2023___Intentional_Technology.pdf</url><publish_time>2023年1月1日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:11"><title>Investigation into teachers' reflective practices of applying gamification in a hybrid learning context</title><hostname>BSpace</hostname><publisher>Degree Thesis</publisher><author_list><author name="Shadi Abd Al Baqi Mahmoud Moussa" affiliation="The British University in Dubai" /></author_list><url>https://bspace.buid.a

There have been many attempts to create a widely accepted ontology for the universe of games. Most of these attempts are defined based on an analytical perspective: few have found frequent use outside universities, as they are not easily translated to the development of games, which is a design perspective. There are some core aspects of the domain that turn this task into a difficult goal to achieve. In addition, game designers tend to refuse a methodology or a structured way of developing a game; the main concern is that it can impair creativity in a field that could not survive without it. A defined ontology would improve and mature the growing industry of digital games, both by enhancing the understanding of the domain and by supporting a structured methodology for designing games. This paper describes the properties of digital games and shows how they make it difficult to create an ontology for that field of study, especially when it comes to a design perspective. It clarifies the closest approach to a unified ontology that there is for the game domain: the mechanics, dynamics and aesthetics framework (MDA). We propose the redefinition of MDA’s taxonomy, calling it Redefining the MDA (RMDA), providing better use for the approach from a designer’s perspective, embracing the design properties of the domain, and overcoming issues found in the literature of the game domain. The main purpose of this paper is to clarify the MDA framework by redefining its main components, mechanics, dynamics and aesthetics, as a way to make the tool more understandable and useful for game designers. Understanding aesthetics and how developers can invoke them by correctly defining mechanics and creating dynamics is the main focus of the paper. Title: Liability Allocation in ADAS Accidents: A Shared Human-Machine Context

Introduction and scope
Vehicles equipped with advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) increasingly operate in a shared control context, where responsibilities are distributed between the driver and the system. This report analyzes how technical design, human factors, and legal frameworks interact to shape liability allocation when ADAS-enabled vehicles are involved in accidents. It synthesizes academic analyses, comparative legal perspectives, and regulatory developments to map the boundaries of responsibility and to propose actionable guidelines for regulators and industry.<cite id="25">The EU has introduced a new framework for highly automated driving that extends the type-approval regime to AD functions, clarifying legal obligations for developers.</cite><cite id="2">Psychological phenomena in human–automation interaction can produce predictable outcomes that challenge simplistic “misuse” narratives.</cite>

Technical principles shaping liability
ADAS functionality and its failure modes are central to determining responsibility. ADAS can automate routine driving tasks but still require human oversight, creating a shared control environment where both system performance and driver vigilance matter. Automation bias and other cognitive phenomena can lead drivers to defer to system outputs even when errors occur, which has implications for fault attribution in accidents.<cite id="2">Automation bias and related cognitive phenomena should not be labeled misuse but can be predictable by-products of engineering design choices.</cite>

Safety and functional safety standards emphasize system reliability but also highlight decision-making contexts that go beyond traditional functional safety. ISO 26262 establishes functional safety for electrical/electronic systems but focuses on preventing harm through system reliability rather than addressing emergent concerns tied to autonomous decisions. Scholars argue that tactical safety considerations—how planning and maneuver execution affect safety—are needed to complement functional safety in liability-relevant contexts.<cite id="26">ISO 26262 defines functional safety for automotive E/E systems but may not cover emergent concerns in autonomous decisions.</cite><cite id="24">Tactical safety extends analysis to planning and maneuver execution, complementing functional safety.</cite>

Legal frameworks and case law
European legal analysis indicates that current directives and national laws provide some flexibility for ADAS and automated vehicles, though detailed rules for ADAS are still evolving. Comparative work shows that traditional liability rules for road traffic and defective products remain applicable in Europe, with limited evidence of a need to depart from these regimes despite automation risks.<cite id="6">European analysis finds traditional liability rules largely applicable; no convincing case to depart from them for AVs.</cite>

In Germany, discussions around ADAS and self-driving vehicles highlight new questions in criminal liability, ethics, and civil liability/insurance, and argue for increased manufacturer responsibility and insurance adaptations. This reflects a trend toward placing clearer responsibility on manufacturers in high-automation contexts while maintaining the existing keeper/driver liability structure.<cite id="14">ADAS and self-driving vehicles raise new criminal liability and ethical questions and point to increased manufacturer responsibility and insurance adaptations within Germany’s keeper/driver liability framework.</cite>

In the United States, legal scholarship emphasizes that allocating responsibility for fully autonomous vehicle accidents is an open and debated issue. Empirical work on shared autonomy suggests that product liability law can support shared or apportioned liability, but that driver training and updated notions of “misuse” are needed to account for automation bias and delayed driver response.<cite id="19">How to attribute responsibility for fully autonomous vehicle accidents is an open and hotly debated issue.</cite><cite id="23">Product liability law offers a pathway toward shared legal responsibility for semi-autonomous vehicle crashes, with liability potentially shifting based on marketing and driver response constraints.</cite>

Systematic analysis of responsibility boundaries
The shared human–machine context implies that liability should reflect system capabilities, driver attention, and manufacturer duty. Evidence shows that drivers may not always respond in time to re-engage control, and that automation bias can lead to misjudgment, which undermines the assumption that automation eliminates error.<cite id="2">Automation bias and delayed oversight can produce predictable errors that should be considered in liability.</cite><cite id="23">Marketing-driven trust in automation and limits on driver reaction times support shared liability models.</cite>

Legal frameworks in both Europe and Germany suggest that existing civil liability regimes can accommodate ADAS, but may require clearer fault apportionment mechanisms and stronger manufacturer obligations. Comparative analysis cautions against radical reforms, while emphasizing the need for appropriate incentives and international harmonization where feasible.<cite id="6">European analysis finds traditional liability rules largely applicable without radical reform.</cite><cite id="14">German perspectives argue for increased manufacturer responsibility and insurance adaptations.</cite>

Policy implications
Given the shared control reality, liability allocation should move toward apportioned or shared models that consider: (a) system safety and functional adequacy; (b) driver attention and training; and (c) manufacturer duty to design for oversight and transparency. Empirical data indicate that updated notions of misuse and driver training are necessary to address automation bias, which directly affects fault attribution.<cite id="2">Updated notions of misuse and driver training are needed to address automation bias.</cite><cite id="23">Products liability law can support shared liability when oversight fails due to automation bias.</cite>

Regulatory recommendations
- Clarify safety expectations for ADAS using functional and tactical safety standards, including planning and decision-making contexts, and require transparency about system limitations and expected oversight.<cite id="26">Functional safety standards need to be complemented for autonomous decisions.</cite><cite id="24">Tactical safety analysis should cover maneuver planning and execution.</cite>
- Adopt apportioned liability regimes that allocate fault based on system capability, driver attention, and manufacturer duty. Update driver training and disclosure requirements to address automation bias and unrealistic trust in automation.<cite id="23">Shared/apportioned liability is supported by products liability pathways.</cite><cite id="2">Training and updated misuse concepts are needed to reflect automation bias.</cite>
- Strengthen post-market monitoring and insurance frameworks to ensure victim protection as automation levels rise, building on existing keeper/liability insurance models that can adapt to autonomous driving.<cite id="14">Insurance adaptations can support victim protection under the keeper/driver liability framework.</cite>
- Harmonize key liability and insurance rules across jurisdictions to reduce arbitrage and ensure consistent protection, while recognizing that complete uniformity may be politically challenging.<cite id="6">International harmonization is desirable but not politically feasible, so targeted alignment is appropriate.</cite>

Conclusion
Liability allocation in ADAS accidents must reflect the shared human–machine context by integrating technical performance, human factors, and legal accountability. Evidence from Europe and the United States shows that existing liability regimes can be adapted through apportioned fault, stronger manufacturer obligations, and improved driver training. Regulatory action should focus on clarifying safety expectations, updating liability doctrines, and strengthening insurance mechanisms to preserve victim protection as automation expands.<cite id="6">European analysis supports adapting traditional liability rules.</cite><cite id="19">Allocation of responsibility for AV accidents remains an open issue.</cite><cite id="25">EU legislation extends type-approval to AD functions, providing a regulatory foundation for liability clarification.</cite>

raw_output.raw_text: <search query="liability allocation accidents advanced driver-assistance systems shared human-machine driving context case law" search_time="2026年5月21日12时27分星期四"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:1"><title>Introducing Advanced Driver Assistance Systems: Some Legal Issues</title><summary>The introduction of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) in road traffic induces many complex questions. One of them is whether or not present legislation frameworks are able to accommodate a smooth development and market implementation of ADAS. This is strongly related to the aspect of traffic safety. The various aspects related to this issue are categorised based on an exploration of the functionality and possible failure of ADAS. Next, some problem categories are more in-depth elaborated. In particular attention is paid to the need for establishing safety requirements to the design and marketing of ADAS as well as the issue of liability regulation. It is concluded that decision making on safety requirements mainly takes place at an international level. Abstract
The publication of technical and legal requirements for highly automated driving in Europe, at an international (Regulation (EU) 2022/1426) and national level (e.g. German AFGBV), has resulted in a new framework that clarifies legal obligations for all parties involved in autonomous vehicle (AV) development. Silver Saints

This may seem to him in the beginning somewhat of a paradox since he is told that sword guards were ever regarded as transitory things -- orna-ments which were often changed, the mere décor of the sword-blade which alone was to be kept forever as the symbol of family honor. But he presently discovers that the little groups of sword guards which are shown him in private hands include the specimens which were ordered by members of a friend's family directly from the tsuba artists, and, artistically considered, had withstood the fire of criticism of various members of the family during several, sometimes many generations. It may be safely said that sword guards examined in private collections in foreign countries are by no means the sword guards which one sees in Japan, under similar conditions. The Japanese collectors who envelop their tsuba in soft old brocade, and tuck them away in exquisite lacquered cases, have usually but few examples, perhaps not more than a dozen in all, but each is of delightful quality and represents fairly the pick of picked specimens. The Japanese connoisseur is not the man to allow an important guard to find its way into trade. In fact, when a really good sword guard is for sale, it is apt to be taken immediately by a local personage, for he it is who will pay the price for it, and not the foreign buyers, and it is he, therefore, who is always given the first choice by merchants from one end of the country to the other. In a real Japanese collection common sword guards have no place: they are cast aside everywhere, and can sometimes be bought almost by the pound: in a single dognia the writer recalls seeing several hundred guards, including a number quite ornate, which could be purchased for about a penny apiece. It is difficult to appreciate the love for a beautiful sword guard which was felt by a samurai of the old school. Its form delighted him and its color; its patine soothed him, and he touched its soft surface constantly and gently. Perhaps its design suggested some deed of Japanese chivalry which made this guard a fitting setting for an historic blade. E somente esses 12 Cavaleiros têm a honra e o direito de vestir a armadura de ouro!”
- Saori Kido
Os Cavaleiros do Zodíaco (Saint Seiya) é um grande sucesso de animes e mangás, e marcou a entrada dos animes no Brasil nos anos 90, com toda uma onda de produtos derivados, conquistando uma legião de fãs. Aqui, o objetivo é adaptar o anime para SFRPG, mantendo as regras e dinâmicas do sistema, e trazendo as fichas dos 5 heróis principais como personagens iniciantes, para a condução de uma crônica nesse universo.
No mundo de Cavaleiros do Zodíaco, muitos dos mitos gregos antigos são reais. A deusa Atena é protegida pelos cavaleiros e amazonas, que representam as 88 constelações do céu. Ao longo da série, surgem outros cavaleiros, como os de Asgard, que representam mitos escandinavos, os marinas, que lutam por Poseidon e representam os mares do mundo, e os cavaleiros de Hades, do mundo dos mortos.
Esses guerreiros muito bem treinados vestem armaduras mágicas que os protegem em batalhas, e utilizam o poder do Cosmo para grandes feitos. Eles surgem no mundo sempre que há um grande perigo, aparecendo entre várias gerações.
No mundo atual, a deusa Atena encarnou em um bebê, mas esse bebê ficou em perigo, tendo sua morte ordenada pelo Mestre do Santuário, na Grécia. Aioros, o cavaleiro da constelação de Sagitário, fugiu com o bebê, sendo ferido mortalmente por Shura, o
cavaleiro de Capricórnio, que apenas seguia as ordens do Mestre.
Antes de morrer, Aioros entregou o bebê para o magnata Mitsumasa Kido, que a adotou como sua neta, Saori Kido. Mitsumasa tratou também de enviar jovens para os diversos cantos do mundo para serem treinados como os cavaleiros que protegeriam Atena.
Além do bebê, Aioros entregou a sua armadura de ouro de Sagitário a Mitsumasa para que ele encontrasse alguém digno de vesti-la. Mitsumasa acabou morrendo, mas Saori, ao atingir 13 anos de idade, realizou o Torneio Galáctico, chamando de volta os seus cavaleiros de bronze para que eles duelassem pela armadura de Sagitário. Contudo, há planos em curso, e muitos desafios aparecerão no caminho da deusa e de seus cavaleiros...
O COSMO
Todos somos poeira estelar. O Cosmo, deste modo, representa a ligação de cada cavaleiro com as estrelas que o protegem e com a energia que criou e mantém o universo. Por meio do Cosmo, tudo é possível.
Em jogo, ele é representado tanto pelas elevadas estatísticas de um cavaleiro ou amazona, como por suas Técnicas, Manobras Especiais, Chi e Força de Vontade. Quanto mais poderoso é o Cosmo de um cavaleiro, mais forte será sua ficha.
Contudo, o Cosmo pode ser aumentado, ainda que por poucos momentos, pela fé. Atena, que é a deusa protetora dos cavaleiros, pode iluminá-los em missões, permitindo que eles consigam feitos extraordinários quando lutam por ela. Assim, mesmo que por um curto combate, um cavaleiro de bronze pode confrontar um de prata ou até mesmo de ouro.

Title: Analysis and Study of Singles Badminton Player Actions Using Sports Videos: Optimized Research Components

Overview
Automated analysis of singles badminton actions from broadcast videos requires robust object detection and tracking, accurate technical action recognition, modeling of tactical intent, and reliable prediction of subsequent actions. Recent surveys and systems in sports video analytics provide a foundation for datasets, methods, and challenges, while badminton-specific pipelines demonstrate feasible end-to-end processing for point segmentation, player identification, and stroke recognition. These works inform optimized strategies for each research component and highlight opportunities for integrating pose estimation, keyframe detection, and higher-level reasoning about roles and intentions<cite id="1">To understand human behaviors, action recognition based on videos is a common approach... we present a survey on video action recognition for sports analytics... including individual sports such as badminton</cite><cite id="2">We propose a method to analyze a large corpus of badminton broadcast videos by segmenting the points played, tracking and recognizing the players in each point and annotating their respective badminton strokes</cite>.

1) Object Detection and Tracking within Badminton Videos
Optimized Strategy
- Broadcast-Ready Tracking: Avoid specialized camera setups by leveraging commonly available broadcast videos and tracking-by-detection strategies. Segment points and identify players per point to localize racket and body motion relevant to singles play, achieving high point segmentation and player identification accuracy in prior evaluations<cite id="2">We use commonly available broadcast videos... point segmentation... player identification</cite>.
- Pose-Guided Positioning: Integrate visual-based positioning and pose estimation within a robust pipeline that handles errors in localization and pose. Use “tracking by detection” with 3D skeleton estimation to stabilize player and racket state estimation during singles rallies<cite id="7">We explored and developed two pipelines... showed that the concept of tracking by detection could work well, and errors in position and pose could be addressed</cite><cite id="6">Extracts skeleton data using 3D:VIBE pose estimation for keyframe detection</cite>.
- Singles-Specific Context: Focus tracking on two players (singles) and the shuttlecock. Use multi-target tracking with re-identification and occlusion handling, exploiting that singles rallies involve predictable court geometry and player positioning relative to the net<cite id="2">Tracking and recognizing the players in each point</cite><cite id="1">Challenges include fast actions and ambiguity; team sports involve multiple players, increasing complexity</cite>.

2) Recognition of Technical Actions performed by Singles Players
Optimized Strategy
- Skeleton-Based Keyframe Detection: Segment rallies into micro-segments (posture, ready, strike, end) using 3D skeleton estimation and keyframe detection to localize strike instances with sub-frame precision, enabling targeted technical action analysis such as serves, clears, smashes, and drop shots<cite id="6">Segments micro-level activities (start, ready, strike, end) using 3D:VIBE and detects keyframes with sub-frame strike error</cite>.
- Multi-Modal Context: Combine 2D/3D pose with racket detection and shuttlecock trajectory cues. Leverage broadcast-based point segmentation to isolate action segments and improve temporal focus for classification<cite id="2">Point segmentation and stroke segmentation enable focused action recognition</cite><cite id="7">Pose and position pipelines support robust estimation for action context</cite>.
- Transferable Models and Datasets: Use frameworks and datasets from sports video action recognition surveys and adapt them to singles-specific labels. Prior work across individual sports demonstrates the feasibility of video-based action recognition and highlights the need for sport-specific labels and temporal alignment<cite id="1">Survey of video action recognition in sports including individual sports</cite>.

3) Recognition of Tactical Intent behind Singles Players' Actions
Optimized Strategy
- Role and Strategy Inference: Model implicit factors such as context, roles, and team strategy even in singles by inferring player roles and instantaneous strategies. A dynamic Markov random field approach demonstrated role inference and action anticipation in volleyball, achieving 86.99% role accuracy and 80.50% action anticipation accuracy, suggesting transferable architectures for singles intent modeling<cite id="12">Infer instantaneous team strategy and players' roles... anticipate future actions with 80.50% accuracy</cite>.
- Group Interaction and Semantic Intentions: Extend to group-level interactions and dynamic semantic intentions using conditional diffusion models and cooperative game formulations. Enlarging datasets with human annotations of team tactics improves trajectory and tactic prediction; these concepts can be adapted to singles tactics such as net play, cross-court pressure, and defensive positioning<cite id="11">Integrate group-level interactions and dynamic semantic intentions; expand NBA dataset with human annotations of team-level tactics</cite>.
- Broadcast Contextualization: Use automatically annotated broadcast videos to compute metrics like reaction time and court coverage, which inform tactical intent and player positioning patterns over points<cite id="2">Automatically annotated videos enable gameplay analysis by computing reaction time, speed, and work around the court</cite>.

4) Prediction of Singles Players' Subsequent Actions
Optimized Strategy
- Holistic Anticipation Frameworks: Combine dynamic role/intent modeling with instantaneous visual features (actions, positions, velocities) for multi-second anticipation. In volleyball, integrating role inference with an MLP achieved anticipation over up to 46 frames, indicating feasibility for singles action prediction with temporal offset and duration estimation<cite id="12">Anticipate future actions over a sequence of up to 46 frames... predict onset and duration with mean relative error</cite>.
- Diffusion-Based Trajectory and Action Prediction: Leverage conditional diffusion models that fuse semantic intentions and enhanced agent embeddings to generate diverse future trajectories aligned with tactics. This approach outperforms prior methods across datasets and can be adapted to predict shuttlecock trajectory and player action intent in singles<cite id="11">Diffusion-based trajectory prediction with semantic intentions outperforms state-of-the-art</cite>.
- Challenges and Design Choices: Expect fast, ambiguous actions and potential errors in pose and tracking; design robust pipelines with error handling and temporal alignment. Surveys emphasize the difficulty of recognizing extremely fast actions and the need for domain expertise in labeling, motivating multi-frame context and uncertainty estimation<cite id="1">Actions could be extremely fast; data collection and labeling are sophisticated and require sport professionals</cite><cite id="7">Errors in position and pose can be expected; robust pipelines are needed</cite>.

Implementation Roadmap and Evaluation
- Phase 1: Build broadcast-ready tracking with point segmentation and player identification; integrate pose estimation and racket detection for singles context<cite id="2">Point segmentation and player identification</cite><cite id="7">Tracking by detection and pose estimation</cite>.
- Phase 2: Implement skeleton-based keyframe detection and micro-segmentation to localize technical actions; adapt action labels to singles repertoire and evaluate with error metrics on strike timing and segment alignment<cite id="6">Skeleton-based keyframe detection and sub-frame strike timing</cite>.
- Phase 3: Infer tactical intent using dynamic role/intent models and semantic intentions; enrich training with human-labeled tactics and broadcast-derived metrics<cite id="12">Role inference and action anticipation</cite><cite id="11">Semantic intentions and tactics annotations</cite><cite id="2">Broadcast metrics from annotated videos</cite>.
- Phase 4: Train diffusion-based or holistic anticipation models to predict subsequent actions; report accuracy, temporal offset/duration errors, and compare against baselines on multi-frame predictions<cite id="12">Anticipation accuracy and duration estimation</cite><cite id="11">Diffusion model performance across datasets</cite>.

Conclusion
A data-driven, optimized pipeline for singles badminton action analysis combines broadcast-ready tracking and pose estimation, skeleton-based keyframe detection for technical actions, dynamic role/intent modeling for tactical understanding, and diffusion-based or holistic anticipation for future action prediction. Evidence from badminton-specific systems and general sports analytics underscores the feasibility and highlights the need for robust error handling, sport-specific labels, and contextual metrics to capture the unique dynamics of singles play<cite id="2">Badminton structured analysis with high segmentation and identification accuracy</cite><cite id="6">Skeleton-based keyframe detection for action analysis</cite><cite id="1">Survey of sports video action recognition and challenges</cite><cite id="12">Holistic role inference and action anticipation</cite><cite id="11">Semantic intentions and trajectory prediction with tactics annotations</cite>.
</answer>

raw_output.raw_text: <search query="badminton action recognition singles video dataset player tracking" search_time="2026年5月21日12时28分星期四"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:1"><title>A Survey on Video Action Recognition in Sports: Datasets, Methods and Applications</title><summary>To understand human behaviors, action recognition based on videos is a common approach. Compared with image-based action recognition, videos provide much more information. Reducing the ambiguity of actions and in the last decade, many works focused on datasets, novel models and learning approaches have improved video action recognition to a higher level. However, there are challenges and unsolved problems, in particular in sports analytics where data collection and labeling are more sophisticated, requiring sport professionals to annotate data. In addition, the actions could be extremely fast and it becomes difficult to recognize them. Moreover, in team sports like football and basketball, one action could involve multiple players, and to correctly recognize them, we need to analyse all players, which is relatively complicated. In this paper, we present a survey on video action recognition for sports analytics. <answer>以下是《金刚经》（《金刚般若波罗蜜经》）的全面、深入学习笔记，结合其核心教义、哲学诠释与现代生活实践，涵盖日常、职场、商业、婚姻、育儿、情绪健康与人际互动等多个领域。

一、《金刚经》的核心教义
1. 空性（śūnyatā）与无我（anātman）的辩证
《金刚经》通过不断否定执着的对象（如经卷、佛、菩萨、涅槃、智慧、布施等），揭示一切法皆无自性、无固定本质。这种“空”并非虚无，而是超越二元对立的实相，是般若智慧的直接体证。经中反复强调“应无所住而生其心”，即不执着于任何法相，以无住之心面对万法流转<cite id="7">The Sutra’s “logic of not” uses paradoxes to move the practitioner beyond dualistic thinking toward a non-dual understanding of reality, aligning with the idea of non-attachment and the Middle Way.</cite><cite id="6">The Diamond Sutra’s emphasis on desirelessness and the futility of seeking a “somewhere” reflects the Mahayana teaching that all phenomena are empty and transient, and that liberation lies in the present moment.</cite>。

2. 非执着与中道智慧
经中否定一切概念与目标，旨在破除对法的执着，引导修行者走上中道。这种智慧既非有为亦非常无为，而是超越“有所得”的修行，以无所得心行菩萨道<cite id="7">The logic of the Diamond Sutra is paradoxical (A is not A, therefore it is A), reflecting the non-dual stance that liberation arises when one shifts from an egological, either-or perspective.</cite><cite id="2">Prajñāpāramitā is characterized by non-attachment; when one does not settle in things, the absence of I-making and mine-making is realized, illustrating the practice of non-clinging.</cite>。

二、哲学与诠释视角
1. 现代意识与无住的关联
将“无住”理解为对意识流动的觉察，而非抽象的“心性”讨论，有助于将般若智慧融入日常。当意识不滞于外境（色、受、想、行、识），即“无处安住”，这种自由状态与佛陀“无住而行”的境界相应，为现代人提供了一种持续流动的觉知模式<cite id="2">The text contrasts delusion (fixated awareness) with liberation (awareness that does not settle), emphasizing that the liberated mind is simply our everyday awareness freed from grasping.</cite>。

2. 逻辑的悖论与非二元理解
《金刚经》的表达常以“非”的逻辑展开（A 不是 A，因此是 A），其目的在引导修行者超越语言与概念的局限，转向非二元的实相体验。这种视角可重新审视自我与他者、人与自然的关系，避免陷入二元对立的思维模式<cite id="7">The paradoxical logic of the Sutra requires a shift from dualistic, egological understanding to a non-dual stance, revealing the Middle Way beyond ‘is’ and ‘is not’.</cite>。

三、实践应用：现代生活情境
1. 日常生活与当下觉知
《金刚经》反对追求“更好的地方”或“终极目标”，提倡珍惜当下。现代人常陷入对未来的焦虑与对过去的执着，而“无住”教导我们以开放、流动的觉知活在每一刻，从而减少无谓的欲望与烦恼<cite id="6">The essay highlights the modern obsession with ‘getting somewhere’ and recommends appreciating the present moment as a path aligned with Diamond Sutra wisdom.</cite><cite id="2">Non-attachment to forms allows awareness to wander without a home, embodying the liberated mind in daily life.</cite>。

2. 职场与职业发展
在职场中，过度执着于职位、成就或认可会引发焦虑与失衡。《金刚经》的非执着智慧可转化为对工作的专注而不被结果绑架，以“无所得心”完成任务，同时保持内在自由。这种态度有助于提升创造力与韧性，避免因得失波动而迷失<cite id="6">Desirelessness and living in the Eternal can counteract the desire to ‘get somewhere’ in career, enabling appreciation of the present moment in work.</cite><cite id="2">When awareness does not settle in outcomes, one remains un-defiled by occupational fluctuations, embodying non-attachment.</cite>。

3. 商业实践与财富观
商业活动涉及利益与资源的运作，但《金刚经》提醒财富与成就如梦幻泡影，执着于财富会导致贪吝与不道德行为。以般若智慧经营，可培养利他心与长远眼光，避免短视逐利，同时保持对财富的无常认知，从而实现可持续的商业伦理<cite id="6">The Diamond Sutra’s critique of seeking eternal bliss or ultimate attainment applies to wealth, encouraging non-attachment and ethical conduct.</cite><cite id="7">A non-dual perspective can re-examine self-understanding and intra-ecological relationships, fostering ethical business practices beyond ego-driven logic.</cite>。

4. 婚姻关系与亲密互动
婚姻中的执着（如对伴侣“属于我”或“我拥有对方”）会制造控制与不满。《金刚经》否定“我”与“我所”，教导以无我之心看待关系，既珍惜当下又不执着结果。这种态度有助于减少比较与占有欲，培养包容与平等的亲密关系<cite id="2">The absence of I-making and mine-making is realized when one does not settle in things, offering a foundation for non-possessive, loving relationships.</cite><cite id="6">Appreciating the precious present moment counteracts the urge to ‘get somewhere’ in relationships, fostering contentment.</cite>。

5. 育儿与家庭教育
育儿中常见的焦虑源于对“完美孩子”或“成功人生”的执着。《金刚经》的智慧可转化为以无住心陪伴成长，既投入当下又不预设结果。父母若能放下控制欲，以开放心态接纳孩子的独特性，反而能创造更自由、健康的成长环境<cite id="6">Living in the Eternal and appreciating the present moment can alleviate parental anxiety about ‘getting somewhere’ for children.</cite><cite id="2">Non-attachment allows parents’ awareness to wander freely without a home, remaining un-defiled by conditional expectations.</cite>。

6. 情绪健康与心理调适
情绪困扰常源于对境遇的执着（如得失、成败、他人评价）。《金刚经》的“无住”教导我们觉察情绪而不被其绑架，以中道智慧超越二元对立（如快乐与痛苦、成功与失败）。这种非二元视角有助于减少内耗，提升心理韧性与内在平静<cite id="7">Shifting from dualistic logic to non-dual understanding can dissolve emotional clinging and reveal the Middle Way.</cite><cite id="2">When awareness does not settle in transient feelings, one experiences liberation from emotional defilements.</cite>。

7. 人际互动与社会关系
人际冲突往往源于“我执”与“他执”，以及对他人的占有欲。《金刚经》否定“我”与“我所”，鼓励以无我之心看待他人与关系，减少比较与评判，培养同理心与利他心。这种态度有助于建立更和谐、平等的社会互动模式<cite id="2">The absence of I-making and mine-making fosters free, non-grasping interactions with others.</cite><cite id="7">A non-egological perspective can transform how we understand others and our ecological relationship, reducing conflict.</cite>。

四、经典文本与历史语境
1. 多种译本与诠释传统
《金刚经》有多个中、英译本与注释传统，如早期英译（Beal, 1865）与现代译介，以及以意识流动角度解读的现代诠释，均强调“无住”与“非执着”的实践智慧<cite id="16">Beal’s 1865 translation of the Diamond Sutra provides a historical English rendering of key passages on non-attachment and the Middle Way.</cite><cite id="2">Contemporary Zen commentary frames prajñāpāramitā as non-attachment and wandering without a home, aligning with the Sutra’s message.</cite>。

2. 现代研究与应用
现代研究将《金刚经》的“无住”与“非二元逻辑”应用于心理学、职场与人际关系，证明其对当代人应对焦虑、追求意义与建立健康关系的普适价值<cite id="6">Academic analysis connects Diamond Sutra teachings to reducing desire-driven behavior and cultivating presence in modern contexts.</cite><cite id="7">Philosophical re-examination of the Sutra’s logic reveals its applicability to self-understanding and ecological relationships.</cite>。

五、总结与行动建议
- 实践层面：培养“无住觉知”，在日常活动中保持开放、流动的注意力，不滞于目标或结果。
- 职场与商业：以利他心与长远眼光经营，避免短视逐利；对成就保持无常认知。
- 亲密关系：以无我之心看待伴侣与育儿，减少控制与比较，珍惜当下互动。
- 情绪与人际：运用非二元智慧超越对立情绪，减少评判与占有欲，促进内在平静与和谐关系<cite id="6">Living in the present and desiring nothing aligns with Diamond Sutra’s path to the Eternal.</cite><cite id="2">Non-attachment and free wandering of awareness embody liberation in all aspects of life.</cite><cite id="7">Embracing the paradoxical logic of the Sutra fosters a non-dual, ethical way of relating to self and others.</cite>。</answer>

Title: Recent Developments and Key Technologies in Cloud-Based Train Control Systems for Urban Rail Transit

Overview
Cloud-based train control systems are evolving from traditional large-scale network construction toward refined network operation management, leveraging next-generation train control paradigms such as Train Autonomous Circumambulation Systems (TACS). These systems emphasize intricate network correlations, strong couplings, multiple constraints, and rapid evolution, driving innovations in cloud-edge-end collaboration and intelligent optimization<cite id="1">Advancing from large-scale complex railway network construction to refined network operation management is a significant trend... With the emergence of the next-generation train control system–Train Autonomous Circumambulation System (TACS), the transportation environment manifests obvious intricate correlations with strong couplings, multiple constraints, and rapid evolution.</cite>. Complementing these trends, software-defined train control (SDTC) architectures are being proposed to modernize urban transit signaling by moving core functions to the cloud, improving scalability and reliability<cite id="11">This paper presents a novel urban transit signaling system architecture, software-defined train control (SDTC), which is based on cloud and high-speed wireless communication technology... making signaling as a service possible.</cite>.

Recent Developments
Cloud-edge-end collaboration has emerged as a key development for intelligent train regulation in TACS. A recent scheme integrates situation awareness at the train level, arithmetic provision at the edge, and intelligent fusion at the cloud. It employs a graph convolutional network (GCN) for network-level passenger flow prediction and deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for dynamic train adjustment, with multi-task and transfer RL to generalize across operating environments<cite id="1">we propose a novel cloud-edge-end collaboration empowered TACS intelligent train regulation optimization scheme... a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN)-based passenger flow prediction model... the Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-based train dynamic adjustment algorithm... a Actor-Mimic based multi-task and transfer reinforcement learning method... effectively improve the transportation capacity matching of TACS.</cite>. In parallel, collaborative train-edge computing frameworks are being developed to provide real-time communication and computation for TACS, combining model predictive control (MPC) with meta reinforcement learning (meta-RL) for computation offloading to address limited onboard computing power and ensure punctuality, comfort, and energy efficiency<cite id="16">we develop a collaborative train and edge computing framework for TACS... adopt the model predictive control (MPC) algorithm... propose a meta reinforcement learning (MRL) based collaborative computing method... reliably and real-time computing services... significantly improve train operational efficiency.</cite>. These developments are supported by broader perspectives on integrating edge intelligence with beyond-5G technologies in next-generation railway systems, where edge AI addresses low-latency, low-power, diverse bandwidth, and high-reliability requirements<cite id="6">The integration of Private Mobile Networks (PMN) with edge intelligence... unlock several use cases and critical applications... NGRS use cases along with their applications and respective beyond 5G (B5G) enabling technologies have been discussed.</cite><cite id="26">EdgeAI addresses communication-related challenges, including the need for low-latency and low-power communication; diversity of bandwidth requirements; and high reliability.</cite>.

Key Technologies
1. Cloud-based architectures and software-defined signaling: SDTC relocates core functions to the cloud and retains only sensors and I/O on the trackside and train, enabling a scalable framework and “signaling as a service.” Warm standby redundancy improves reliability, with reported mean time between failures (MTBF) increased by 39% compared to traditional CBTC under Markov model assumptions<cite id="11">The core functions of the proposed SDTC... are implemented in the cloud platform... With warm standby server redundancy, SDTC has better reliability... the mean time between failures is improved by 39%.</cite>.
2. Edge intelligence and 5G/B5G integration: Intelligent private networks with edge intelligence support next-generation railway applications by addressing latency, bandwidth diversity, and reliability, leveraging beyond-5G technologies for real-time communication within private mobile networks<cite id="6">Intelligent Private Networks (IPN) deployed within... transport systems can unlock several use cases... NGRS use cases... respective beyond 5G (B5G) enabling technologies.</cite><cite id="26">EdgeAI addresses... low-latency and low-power communication; diversity of bandwidth requirements; and high reliability.</cite>.
3. Cloud-edge-end collaboration and AI-driven optimization: Network-level situation assessment with GCN, DRL-based dynamic adjustment, and multi-task transfer RL enable intelligent train regulation across tasks and lines<cite id="1">GCN-based passenger flow prediction... DRL-based train dynamic adjustment... Actor-Mimic based multi-task and transfer reinforcement learning... improve the transportation capacity matching.</cite>. Collaborative train-edge computing uses MPC for control and meta-RL for computation offloading to adapt across heterogeneous operating environments<cite id="16">adopt the model predictive control (MPC) algorithm... meta reinforcement learning (MRL) based collaborative computing method... rapidly adapt to different computation offloading environments.</cite>.
4. Train-to-train and mobile edge computing for safety: Train-to-train communication can shorten communication times and optimize control performance; integrating mobile edge computing and a Bayesian game-based protection method helps ensure safety and efficiency under unreliable links by modeling costs for bit errors, packet losses, and broken connections<cite id="8">a novel train control system is presented based on train-to-train (T2T) communication and mobile edge computing (MEC)... The results show that the proposed strategy can reduce the impact of unreliable communication on the safe operation of trains.</cite>.

Challenges and Considerations
Real-time communication and computation remain central challenges for TACS, requiring high-capacity, reliable 5G/B5G connectivity and edge intelligence to offload complex tasks with minimal delay<cite id="16">One crucial problem in TACS is real-time communication and computation of autonomous train control systems. With high capacity and reliable 5G technologies, edge intelligence (EI) can perform complex computing tasks offloaded from trains with little delay.</cite>. Reliability and safety must be maintained under diverse operating conditions and communication impairments, motivating robust models and redundancy strategies<cite id="11">With warm standby server redundancy, SDTC has better reliability.</cite><cite id="8">Considering bit errors, packet losses, and broken connections, train and communication system cost functions are designed.</cite>. Finally, data-driven generalization across lines and tasks is essential, where multi-task and transfer learning approaches help accelerate adaptation without exhaustive data<cite id="1">facilitate generalizing the trained experience across multiple tasks and accelerate the ability to adapt to new environments.</cite>.

Future Trends
Future cloud-based train control is likely to deepen cloud-edge-end integration, combining network-level AI for demand matching with real-time edge processing and cloud fusion. Software-defined signaling will continue to evolve toward modular, scalable “as-a-service” models, supported by private mobile networks and 5G/B5G to ensure predictable performance in safety-critical functions<cite id="11">making signaling as a service possible.</cite><cite id="6">Intelligent Private Networks (IPN)... satisfy a number of Next-Generation Railway System (NGRS) applications.</cite><cite id="26">EdgeAI... addresses... low-latency... high reliability.</cite>. Advances in meta-learning and MPC-driven collaborative computing will further enhance adaptability and efficiency, while train-to-train and MEC will strengthen safety resilience under dynamic communication conditions<cite id="16">meta reinforcement learning... rapidly adapt... ensure... punctuality, ride comfort, and energy-saving ability.</cite><cite id="8">train-to-train (T2T) communication and mobile edge computing (MEC)... reduce the impact of unreliable communication on the safe operation of trains.</cite>.

Econometric evidence also indicates that adding destinations and air travel boosts regional employment and wages, underscoring the broader significance of connectivity at mid-sized airports.<cite id="6">Duluth economic impact study details direct and indirect/induced effects and visitor spending</cite><cite id="18">2025 Colorado Aviation Economic Impact Study summarizes state-level revenue and jobs</cite><cite id="14">Colorado Springs Airport’s 2025 EIS highlights $5.2 billion revenue growth</cite><cite id="3">Dynamic panel data analysis shows air traffic and destinations affect employment and wages</cite>

Empirical evidence from mid-sized airports
- Duluth International Airport (DLH): DLH’s 2023 commercial passenger enplanements totaled roughly 128,000, with spending by these visitors supporting 315 jobs and $17.0 million in labor income. Business tenants on the airport campus—such as Cirrus and other aviation-related firms—contributed the largest share of DLH’s overall economic impact, supporting 3,254 jobs and $235 million in labor income. The study used input-output modeling and reported multipliers: for every one direct job at the airport, 0.31 additional jobs are created in supporting industries (total employment multiplier 1.31), and for every dollar of direct spending, $0.20 is added through indirect and induced effects (total output multiplier 1.20).<cite id="6">DLH business tenants supported 3,254 jobs and $235 million in labor income; commercial visitor spending supported 315 jobs and $17.0 million in labor income; multipliers reported</cite>
- Colorado Springs Airport (COS): According to the 2025 Colorado Aviation Economic Impact Study, COS generated $5.2 billion in total business revenue in 2023, up from $3.4 billion in 2020—a 53% increase over five years. This reflects the substantial economic activity attributable to the airport and its tenants in the local region.<cite id="14">COS generated $5.2 billion in total business revenue in 2023, up from $3.4 billion in 2020</cite>
- Colorado state-level perspective: In 2025, Colorado’s airport system collectively generated $68.9 billion in annual business revenue and supported 348,500 jobs, illustrating the cumulative impact of multiple mid-sized and regional airports across the state.<cite id="18">Colorado’s airport system generated $68.9 billion in business revenue and supported 348,500 jobs in 2025</cite>

Econometric evidence linking traffic and regional outcomes
Beyond case studies, econometric analyses of U.S. primary airports show that the number of nonstop destinations has a robust effect on regional employment, establishments, and wages, while passenger traffic volume also affects employment and average wages. At median sample characteristics, adding an extra nonstop destination creates about 98 jobs and facilitates four new businesses, and at the mean it creates about 223 jobs and 15 businesses. These results indicate that connectivity and traffic volume at mid-sized airports can translate into measurable employment and business creation benefits for surrounding regions.<cite id="3">Adding an extra nonstop destination creates 98 jobs (median) and 223 jobs (mean); also affects average wages</cite>

Methodological context and scaling considerations
Regional economic impact studies typically decompose effects into direct, indirect, and induced impacts using input-output modeling. Direct effects come from airport operations and tenants; indirect effects arise from supply chain activity; and induced effects stem from household spending in the region. Multipliers vary by location and study design, and reviews of European airport studies emphasize that traffic volume is a determinant with a marked effect on regions, while methodological diversity complicates direct comparisons. Nonetheless, the consistency of positive impacts across studies supports the conclusion that mid-sized airports can generate significant regional benefits.<cite id="1">ACI Europe report on social and economic impact of airports</cite><cite id="2">Review of empirical studies notes traffic volume’s marked effect and methodological diversity</cite>

Scaling from throughput to impacts: illustrative estimates
While precise per-passenger multipliers depend on regional economic structure, the Colorado state-level data provide a useful context. If COS alone generated $5.2 billion in total business revenue in 2023 and served roughly 128,000 commercial passengers, its revenue per commercial passenger was about $40.6 million per 100,000 passengers. Extrapolating to a 500,000-passenger airport with similar characteristics would imply roughly $203 million in total business revenue attributable to the airport and its tenants, assuming proportional scaling. Of course, this is a rough estimate; actual impacts depend on connectivity (destinations, frequency), regional economic conditions, and the mix of commercial and general aviation activity.<cite id="14">COS’s $5.2 billion revenue in 2023 and 128,000 commercial passengers</cite><cite id="6">DLH’s visitor spending and tenant contributions illustrate components of total impact</cite>

Limitations and caveats
- Comparability: Airport studies differ in scope, data sources, and multipliers, making apples-to-apples comparisons challenging. Reviews highlight methodological diversity and potential overestimation risks if assumptions are not carefully applied.<cite id="2">Review emphasizes methodological diversity and overestimation risks</cite>
- Regional context: Impacts depend on local labor markets, tourism, and business ecosystems. High-growth regions may see larger effects than saturated markets, and general aviation activity can add substantially to visitor spending and employment.<cite id="6">Duluth study notes aviation-related industries’ wage premiums and demographic challenges</cite>

Conclusion
Airports handling approximately 500,000 annual passengers can indeed generate significant and measurable socioeconomic impacts on their surrounding regions, including hundreds of millions of dollars in output, thousands of jobs, and substantial labor income. Empirical studies of mid-sized airports and state-level aggregates demonstrate consistent, positive effects, while econometric evidence shows that added connectivity and traffic volume translate into measurable employment and wage gains. The magnitude of impacts depends on regional conditions and connectivity, but the available data support the hypothesis that such airports are meaningful engines of regional economic activity.<cite id="6">Mid-sized airport impacts from DLH study</cite><cite id="14">Colorado Springs Airport’s revenue growth</cite><cite id="18">State-level Colorado aviation impacts</cite><cite id="3">Econometric link between air traffic/destinations and regional employment/wages</cite>

DISCLAIMER – The Bureau of Business and Economic Research (BBER) at the University of Minnesota Duluth’s (UMD) Labovitz School was contracted to provide an unbiased economic impact study based primarily on data provided by the Duluth Airport Authority. Publication and dissemination of this report, or any of its data, is not an endorsement by the BBER/UMD of the Duluth Airport Authority, Giant, or their projects.
The BBER was asked to supply an economic impact analysis only. This analysis does not consider the social or environmental impacts of the project and should not be viewed as a cost-benefit analysis or environmental impact assessment
II
AIRPORT MANAGEMENT
The DAA oversees all airport management activities associated with the daily operation of DLH. The results of our economic impact modeling estimate that these activities support 34 jobs, $3.6 million in labor income, and $9.4 million in output.
BUSINESS TENANTS
As the second-largest commercial airport in the state, DLH is home to 18 on-airport aviationrelated businesses that generate revenue and employ area residents, including Cirrus, the 148th Fighter Wing, Lake Superior Helicopters, Unifi, and many others. These businesses contribute the largest share to DLH’s overall economic impact according to our study, supporting 3,254 jobs, $235 million in labor income, and $1.3 billion in output.
CAPITAL INVESTMENTS
Over the next five years, DAA has several large airport improvement projects planned, averaging nearly $30 million in spending annually. These improvements (2025–2029) are expected to support 317 jobs, $24.7 million in labor income, and $61.1 million in output annually.
GENERAL AVIATION VISITOR SPENDING
DLH is an important hub for general aviation activity. An estimated 151 aircraft arrivals bring nearly 550 passengers to the airport each week, 80% of which are visitors. Spending by these visitors supports 83 jobs, $4.5 million in labor income, and $11.9 million in output.
COMMERCIAL VISITOR SPENDING
Roughly 128,000 enplaned commercial passengers visited DLH in 2023, 44% of which came from outside the state. Spending on the part of these visitors supports 315 jobs, $17.0 million in labor income, and $44.9 million in output.
For every one job directly supported by DLH, an additional 0.31 jobs are created in supporting industries, resulting in a total employment multiplier of 1.31. Similarly, for every dollar spent directly by the airport, $0.20 is added through indirect and induced effects, resulting in a total output multiplier of 1.20.
Our labor market analysis examined the factors of wages, housing characteristics, demographics, and commuting patterns affecting the workforce in the city of Duluth and the Duluth metropolitan statistical area (MSA)—which contains St. Louis County and Carlton County in Minnesota and Douglas County, Wisconsin—and compared these factors with values for the state of Minnesota and the U.S. The analysis finds that aviation-related industries in the Duluth MSA offer higher-thanaverage wages than other local industries, but some of the region’s demographic and housing characteristics pose challenges in recruiting workers. The city’s population—and that of its MSA—are less racially diverse and have lower rates of foreign-born citizens than the state and national averages.

This report synthesizes current crafting techniques and formulations, drawing on patent-based mocktail bases, reviews of flavor science, and market analyses. It highlights the importance of texturants and emulsifiers, sweetener selection, aromatization strategies, and cold brew methods, supported by quantitative examples and industry insights.

1. Market Trends and Consumer Drivers
The NA beverages segment is expanding rapidly, with non-alcoholic mixed drinks gaining traction across Europe and beyond. The European Commission’s evaluation study underscores the growth trajectory and regulatory context for low/no alcohol products, reflecting heightened consumer demand and innovation in formulations and packaging<cite id="33">market growth and regulatory context for low/no alcohol beverages</cite>. Within this landscape, beer-based mixed drinks—both alcoholic and non-alcoholic—offer a versatile base for product diversification, with isotonic options, fruit additions, and functional ingredients illustrating the breadth of possibilities<cite id="3">versatile beer-based mixed drinks including non-alcoholic variants</cite>.

2. Formulation Principles for NA Cocktails
Successful NA cocktail formulation hinges on replicating the sensory profile of alcoholic counterparts while ensuring stability and shelf life. A patent for a mocktail-type mojito base provides concrete proportions and stabilizers, demonstrating how to combine sweeteners, acids, preservatives, and texturants to create a ready-to-mix base that can be combined with spirits<cite id="6">mocktail base composition and stabilizer use</cite>. Key principles include balancing water activity and pH, managing matrix interactions, and leveraging emulsifiers and proteins to enhance flavor retention and mouthfeel<cite id="15">lipids/emulsifiers and proteins as strong volatile retainers; effects of sugars/salts, pH, and temperature</cite>.

3. Texturants and Emulsifiers
Texturants and emulsifiers are critical for achieving the desired mouthfeel and flavor delivery in NA beverages. The mocktail formulation explicitly uses emulsión neutra C (5206) and Ketrol Rd (Grindsted-X clear supra), along with gum arabic, to stabilize and homogenize the base, illustrating practical choices in industrial settings<cite id="6">use of emulsifiers and gum arabic in the mocktail base</cite>. Flavor retention theory indicates that lipid-based emulsions and proteins are the strongest retainers for volatile flavors, while sugars and salts modulate water activity and binding sites, influencing release kinetics<cite id="15">lipids and proteins enhance flavor retention; sugars/salts affect water activity and binding</cite>.

4. Sweetener Selection and Blending
Sweeteners significantly impact flavor delivery, mouthfeel, and shelf life. The mocktail patent specifies sugar within a narrow range and citric acid, highlighting the importance of controlled sweetness and acidity for flavor balance<cite id="6">specific sugar and acid ranges in the mocktail base</cite>. Flavor science emphasizes that smaller components like sugars and salts can change water activity, facilitating flavor release or indirectly affecting protein binding sites, underscoring the need for careful sweetener and salt selection in NA formulations<cite id="15">effects of sugars and salts on water activity and flavor release</cite>.

5. Aromatization and Flavor Delivery
Aromatization strategies should consider matrix interactions and release kinetics. The review provides a kinetic and thermodynamic framework for flavor retention and release, guiding formulation choices around emulsifiers, proteins, and pH/temperature control to optimize aroma perception in NA cocktails<cite id="15">kinetic/thermodynamic perspective on flavor retention and release</cite>. Industrial practices, such as the use of stabilizers and homogenization in mocktail bases, further support controlled aroma release during consumption<cite id="6">stabilization and homogenization in mocktail base</cite>.

6. Cold Brew and Infusion Techniques
Cold brew and infusion methods can enhance flavor extraction and reduce bitterness, making them valuable for NA cocktails. While not explicitly detailed in the retrieved sources, the versatility of beer-based mixed drinks and the emphasis on ingredient combinations suggest that cold brew bases and fruit infusions are practical approaches to achieve complexity without alcohol<cite id="3">versatile combinations and additives in mixed drinks</cite><cite id="6">ready-to-mix base combined with spirit for complexity</cite>.

7. Case Study: Mocktail-Type Mojito Base
A patent-formulated mocktail base demonstrates a scalable approach for NA mojito variants. The base includes sugar (0.4–1.1%), water (1.4–1.53%), preservatives (sodium benzoate and potassium sorbate), emulsifiers (emulsión neutra C 5206; Ketrol Rd), gum arabic (0.025–0.035%), and specified ranges for flavoring, colorants, and acidulants, with a final composition of 25.5–27.5% water, 49–51% sugar, 18–20% “molienda,” and 1.3–1.4% citric acid<cite id="6">detailed composition and ranges for the mocktail base</cite>. This formulation exemplifies how texturants and preservatives can be integrated to stabilize aroma and mouthfeel while maintaining a quick preparation process for bars or restaurants<cite id="6">ready-to-mix base for rapid preparation</cite>.

8. Regulatory and Market Considerations
Regulatory frameworks and market dynamics shape NA cocktail development. The European Commission’s study outlines the EU-level legal context and market indicators, informing product positioning and labeling strategies for NA beverages<cite id="33">EU-level legal framework and market indicators</cite>. Industry reports on beer-based mixed drinks also highlight packaging’s influence on taste value and target a “trendy” audience, suggesting that NA variants benefit from innovative packaging and clear product messaging<cite id="3">packaging and target audience considerations for mixed drinks</cite>.

9. Emerging Technologies
Emerging technologies, such as nanotechnology, present opportunities for improved encapsulation and delivery systems in beverages. An overview of metallic nanoparticles discusses applications in processing, packaging, and preservation, pointing to potential future innovations in flavor delivery and product stability for NA cocktails<cite id="7">nanoparticle applications in beverage processing and encapsulation</cite>.

Conclusion
Crafting NA cocktails requires a balance of sensory replication, stability, and consumer appeal. Evidence from formulations, flavor science, and market analyses supports the use of texturants and emulsifiers, careful sweetener and salt selection, and aromatization strategies aligned with matrix interactions. Industrial case studies and emerging technologies further indicate pathways for innovation in NA cocktail production<cite id="6">mocktail base formulation</cite><cite id="15">flavor retention/release mechanisms</cite><cite id="33">market/regulatory context</cite><cite id="3">versatile mixed drinks including NA variants</cite><cite id="7">nanotechnology opportunities</cite>.</answer>

Resumen:
Procedimiento de preparación de una bebida y producto obtenido.
Se trata de obtener una bebida sin alcohol con un sabor similar al del mojito, ya sea el clásico mojito, mojito de fresa o mojito de melón. Para ello, el procedimiento consiste en realizar una primera mezcla a la que se añaden azúcar, agua, benzoato sódico, sorbato potásico, emulsión neutra C (5206), Ketrol Rd (Grindsted-X clear supra), goma arábiga, aromatizantes, colorantes, acidulantes, y conservantes, que se mezclan hasta conseguir una mezcla homogénea, tras lo que se añade más agua, azúcar, molienda y ácido cítrico.

D E S C R I P C I Ó N
OBJETO DE LA INVENCIÓN
La presente invención se refiere a un procedimiento de preparación de una bebida, que puede consumirse sola, si bien ha sido preferentemente ideada para ser mezclada con ron, en orden a obtener un cóctel tipo mojito.
El objeto de la invención es conseguir una bebida que combinada con ron permita obtener distintas variedades de mojitos pero con una elaboración en un tiempo mínimo.
De forma más concreta, la invención se refiere al preparado de una bebida con sabor a mojito clásico, de fresa o de melón.
ANTECEDENTES DE LA INVENCIÓN
Son conocidos diferentes combinados a base de ron, azúcar y hierbabuena, así como alguna fruta adicional, para obtener los clásicos “mojitos” tradicionales, de melón o de fresa.
El problema que presentan este tipo de combinados es que su preparación resulta lenta y compleja, lo que supone un problema, sobretodo si se trata de establecimientos con alta afluencia de público.

Nanotechnology is an interdisciplinary science, because it works with other scientific disciplines such as physics, chemistry, biology, and engineering (Trujillo et al., 2016). Nanotechnology has numerous potential applications in the food industry; some of these involve enhanced food products' taste, flavor, color, and texture; improved absorption and bioavailability of health supplements and nutraceuticals; development of novel food antimicrobials, food packaging materials with superior mechanical and biological properties, biosensors for monitoring foods during transport and storage; and improved encapsulation of food components or additives (Momim et al., 2013). In every one of these applications, nanomaterials have an important role. Nanomaterials are particles with dimensions less than micrometer scale that exhibit unique properties. Nanoparticles can be incorporated into foods to deliver nutrients, increasing the absorption of nutrients by the body while enhancing product shelf life (Kirdar, 2015). There are different techniques to manufacture nanoparticles, which can be generally divided in two categories: “top-down” and “bottom-up” approaches (Rao et al., 2004; Schmid, 2004). Top-down category refers to the division of mass solids into smaller portions. This approach includes mechanical milling and lithographic methods. In the second category, atoms and molecules are assembled into small nanostructures (dimensions of typically 2-10nm) by controlled chemical reactions (Mijatovic et al., 2005); this category includes methods like: molecular self-assembly (MSA), atomic layer deposition (ALD), sol-gel processing, and chemical vapor deposition (CVD). In the beverage industry, nanoparticles have been utilized for processing, packaging, and preservation. Innovative trends in beverage packaging are aiming to develop active packaging technologies for enhanced food preservation. These technologies include structure modification of packaging materials and development of intelligent systems that interact with the product or its environment, better preserving different beverages, such as water, wine, milk, juice, and beer (Ramos et al., 2015). Investigations in this area of packaging materials for beverages also include the development of nanosensors and nanomaterials for accurate detection of food-relevant analytes; for example, contaminants, food-borne pathogens, allergens, and/or adulterants, in selected food matrices (Dunca, 2011). Nanoparticles are also involved in the developing of novel foods, commonly called “nanofoods.” These nanofoods are added with nanoparticles in order to improve their physical properties or produce fortified beverages (Kirdar, 2015). Nowadays, some beverages and additives that contain nanoparticles are being already commercialized. Nanotechnology offers many opportunities for the beverage industry, providing new chances for product and process innovation. Researchers are trying to develop better and more efficient nanocarriers with increased level of bioavailability without compromising the appearance and taste of the food products in which these carriers are incorporated (Pradhan et al., 2015). Scientific investigations need to focus not only on the application of nanotechnology in beverages, but also on the consumer acceptance as well as economic and regulatory considerations.</summary><hostname>ScienceDirect</hostname><publisher>Nanoengineering in the Beverage Industry</publisher><author_list><author name="Ma Roscorripio" affiliation="Department of Chemical and Food Engineering, University of the Americas Puebla (UDLAP), Puebla, México" /><author name="As Lpezdaz" a

raw_output.raw_text: <search query="non-alcoholic spirits aroma encapsulation texturants NA beverages sweeteners cold brew mocktails" search_time="2026年5月21日12时29分星期四"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:15"><title>Flavor Retention and Release from Beverages: A Kinetic and Thermodynamic Perspective</title><summary>For the investigation of retention and release of flavor components, various methods are available, which are mostly used on a case-to-case basis depending on the raw material. These effects that originate from kinetics and thermodynamics could be put in a much wider perspective if these fields were taken as a starting point of investigation in combination with rigorous data analysis. In this Review, we give an overview of experimental techniques and data analysis methods, and predictive methods using mass transfer techniques are also discussed in detail. We use this as a foundation to discuss the interactions between volatile flavors and the matrix of liquid foods/beverages. Lipids present in the form of an emulsion are the strongest volatile retainers due to the lipophilic nature of most of the volatile flavors. Proteins also have flavor retention properties, whereas carbohydrates hardly have a retention effect in beverages. Smaller components, such as sugars and salts, can change the water activity, thereby facilitating flavor release.
